form.label: 9. AI Observability & Governance
form.description: A governance-first view of AI usage — cost, latency, and guardrail hits — built to de-risk AI adoption for a leadership team that currently has the handbrake on.

html.blockquote: "AI Observability ist sehr interessant, GL hat da zur Zeit aber etwas die Handbremse drauf, aufgrund Unsicherheit."
html.p: Leadership's hesitation isn't about whether AI is useful — it's about not having visibility and guardrails before it scales: what's being sent to which model, what it costs, whether responses are being checked for sensitive data leakage, and whether usage is auditable. The pitch here isn't "AI observability" as a buzzword — it's specifically the governance layer (cost control, guardrail hits, auditability) that turns "we're not sure" into "we can see exactly what's happening and stop it if needed."

panel.title: Data sources needed to build this for real

ul.li: LLM / API gateway logs — every request to a model provider (Anthropic, OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, etc.) with tokens, latency, cost, and the calling application/team.
Guardrail / DLP scan logs — output from a prompt/response scanner checking for PII, PHI, or policy-violating content before/after the model call.
Model registry / version metadata — which model version answered which request, for reproducibility and rollback if a model update changes behavior.
Identity / access data — which user or service account made each call, so usage and incidents are attributable.

search.query: | makeresults count=4 | streamstats count as i | eval Team=case(i=1,"Radiology-AI-Pipeline",i=2,"Clinical-Docs-Assistant",i=3,"IT-Helpdesk-Bot",i=4,"HR-Screening (pilot, paused)") | eval "Requests"=case(i=1,28400,i=2,14200,i=3,5600,i=4,13) | eval "Spend (CHF)"=case(i=1,712,i=2,398,i=3,161,i=4,13) | table Team "Requests" "Spend (CHF)"

panel.title: Guardrail hits over time — what governance is actually catching

search.query: | makeresults count=3 | streamstats count as i | eval Time=strftime(relative_time(now(), "-".(i*2)."d"), "%Y-%m-%d") | eval Team=case(i=1,"Clinical-Docs-Assistant",i=2,"HR-Screening (pilot, paused)",i=3,"Clinical-Docs-Assistant") | eval Finding=case(i=1,"Response contained unredacted patient name — blocked",i=2,"Prompt contained candidate SSN — blocked, pilot paused",i=3,"Response contained internal-only pricing — blocked") | eval Action=case(i=1,"Blocked, logged, team notified",i=2,"Blocked, pilot escalated to GL",i=3,"Blocked, logged") | table Time Team Finding Action | sort Time

panel.title: The SPL, once the AI gateway + guardrail logs are onboarded

html.pre: index=ai_gateway | stats count as requests, sum(tokens) as tokens, sum(cost_chf) as spend, perc95(latency_ms) as p95_latency by team, model | appendcols [ search index=ai_guardrail action=block | stats count as guardrail_hits by team ] | eval risk_flag=if(guardrail_hits>0, "review", "clear") | table team model requests spend p95_latency guardrail_hits risk_flag | sort - guardrail_hits
html.p: The point for GL: this is a dashboard that shows AI usage and proves the guardrails are catching real things — the evidence needed to move from "handbrake on" to "controlled rollout".
